Spring Boot startup really does multicast context events to @EventListener methods, and ApplicationListenerMethodAdapter evaluates the listener's condition SpEL via EventExpressionEvaluator, so reaching SpelExpression#getValue during SpringApplication.run is a genuine framework flow. The final hop to ConstructorReference#createArray only occurs if an event condition expression contains an array constructor, which is possible but configuration-dependent; the chain itself is a real dispatch path, not a CHA artifact.

This is the canonical Spring4Shell sink chain: a controller's BindingResult.rejectValue triggers AbstractPropertyBindingResult.getActualFieldValue, which resolves properties via BeanWrapperImpl and CachedIntrospectionResults.forClass, exactly the introspection path (CachedIntrospectionResults#<init>/introspectInterfaces) that CVE-2022-22965 exploits. The Petclinic OwnerController.processFindForm genuinely calls rejectValue on a BindingResult, and every hop is a real Spring data-binding call, not a CHA artifact.

exploit_reason: OwnerController#setAllowedFields is a Spring @InitBinder method invoked during binding of externally supplied HTTP form data to the Owner object, so it runs on attacker-controlled requests. It calls the vulnerable WebDataBinder#setDisallowedFields, which is exactly the case-sensitivity flaw (CVE-2022-22968) allowing disallowed fields like 'id' to be set via case variations.
